findings.title: Bootstrap ordinary-handoff failure still has no exact result projection
evidence: BOOTSTRAP-HANDOFF-FAILURE-001 expected is only 'nonsecret failed delivery outcome distinct from GKOS_P6_SECRET_EXPOSURE'. It names neither a concrete bootstrap state/result coordinate with secret_revealed=false nor one exact existing 53-code error envelope.

Its schedule says only 'record failed outcome', and its mutation says only 'handoff evidence only', so the exact response bytes, state advancement or preservation, and exact evidence record are not frozen.

Q14 closes committed credential.issue/rotate post-commit handoff failures, and the credential-family V3 leaves correctly implement that choice, but the distinct bootstrap row remains open and Registry V3 nevertheless declares every row closed.

findings.title: Registry V3 still contains range, unnamed-field, and multi-result executable rows
evidence: ACTIVITY-INTEGER-003, ACTIVITY-INTEGER-004, and ACTIVITY-INTEGER-005 each say 'one integer metadata key' without naming input_bytes, output_bytes, item_count, or result_count. Each ID therefore hides four possible field-specific inputs despite BCI-MECH-005's one-named-field rule.

ANCHOR-INTENT-006 ranges over 'any non-null intent-only field' instead of naming one exact field. COLLISION-ID-EVENT-001 ranges over 'any ID in the four-table global union' instead of fixing the existing collision table and row coordinate.

RESTORE-ABORT-STALE-BINDINGS-001 combines a session, admitted request, cursor, snapshot, and fresh authentication in one ID; its schedule says 'submit each old binding' and its expected field contains distinct session, request/cursor, snapshot, and fresh-auth results.

REDACTION-JSON-001 combines result and error serializers plus multiple sensitive field classes under 'any'; REDACTION-LOG-001 combines all configured log levels and multiple sensitive content classes. These are not one-condition leaves or an explicitly materialized closed parameterization counted as separate executable cases.

RACE-MULTIPROCESS-001 does not name the two distinct mutation operations, the winner, or whether the loser is in a contract-permitted retry class; 'loser retries admission only where contract permits' leaves alternative schedules and outcomes under one ID.

These occurrences survive the registry's declared zero modal/alternative/slash/range shorthand validation because that declared vocabulary profile does not detect generic quantifiers or unnamed field/operation classes.
